A special purpose consent may be granted over a block even if the block is in the licence area of a licence or the consent area of another special purpose consent.
A special purpose consent can only be granted for:
a scientific investigation, or
a reconnaissance survey, or
the collection of small amounts of minerals.
A reconnaissance survey is the exploration of an area to work out whether the area is sufficiently promising to justify more detailed exploration under an exploration licence.

heading.b: Activities authorised by a special purpose consent

block.txt: A special purpose consent holder may:
explore for minerals, and
take samples of or recover minerals,
in the consent area, in accordance with the consent.
Under section 23 (1) the concept of “exploration” extends to activities that are directly related to exploration.
Under section 24 (1) the concept of “recovery” extends to activities that are directly related to the recovery of minerals.
The grant of a consent does not give the consent holder:
any exclusive or proprietary rights over the blocks covered by the consent, or
any option or preference when it comes to the grant of a licence over blocks covered by the consent.
A person may apply to the Minister for a special purpose consent.
The application must:
be made in writing, and
include details of the activities for which consent is being sought, and
specify the blocks for which the consent is being sought.
If the activity involves the collection of only small amounts of minerals (see section 315 (3) (c)), the application must also specify:
any mineral to be recovered, and
the proposed quantity of any mineral to be recovered.
The applicant must pay the appropriate application fee.
The fee must be paid when the application is made.
The Minister may refund any fee paid under subsection (1) but only if the Minister is satisfied that special circumstances exist that justify the refund of the fee.

heading.b: Applicant must obtain agreement of exploration, retention and mining licence holders affected by the application

block.txt: Subject to subsection (3), the applicant must obtain the agreement of interested licence holders to the application.
The agreement must be in writing.
The agreement of an interested licence holder is not necessary if:
the application is for a scientific investigation, and
Australia has obligations under international conventions to allow the investigation.
For the purposes of this section, a licence holder is interested if:
the holder holds an exploration, retention or mining licence, and
the block concerned is inside the licence area.

heading.b: Applicant to notify works licence holders affected by the application

block.txt: The applicant must notify interested works licence holders of the application.
The notification:
must be given to the interested works licence holders in writing, and
must give details of the special purpose consent applied for, and
must invite the interested works licence holder to give comments to the Minister within 30 days after the day on which the notice was given.
For the purposes of this section, a works licence holder is interested if the block concerned is inside the works licence area.
See note 2 to section 3 (1).

heading.b: Minister may grant special purpose consent

block.txt: If the applicant does what is required by sections 318 to 321, the Minister may:
grant a special purpose consent to the applicant, or
refuse the application.
See note 2 to section 3 (1).

heading.b: Matters to be specified in the consent

block.txt: The consent must specify:
the blocks covered by the consent, and
the activities authorised by the consent, and
the period for which the consent is to have effect, and
the consent conditions.
If the activity involves the collection of only small amounts of minerals (see section 315 (3) (c)), the consent must also specify:
the minerals to be collected, and
the quantities to be collected.
The period specified under subsection (1) (c) is not to be more than 12 months.
A consent has effect for the period specified under section 325 (1) (c).
The Minister may grant a special purpose consent subject to whatever conditions the Minister thinks are appropriate.
Without limiting subsection (1), the Minister may impose conditions that relate to:
reports to be provided by the consent holder about activities carried out under the consent, and
environmental matters.
The Minister must keep a register for the purposes of this Part.
The main matters entered in the register are:
the grant or renewal of a licence (see sections 333 and 334),
details of instruments that affect a licence (see section 337),
details of instruments that affect an interest in a licence (see sections 338 and 339),
details of interests in a licence that are acquired by devolution (see section 340),
details of caveats (see section 345).
The register is to be known as the State Offshore Mining Register.
The Minister must keep a document file for the purposes of this Part.
In the document file are to be kept the documents that the Minister is required to keep under this Part.
The documents to be kept in the document file are:
copies of licences (see section 333 (6)),
copies of instruments that affect licences (see section 337 (4)),
copies of transfers of licences (see section 338 (6)),
copies of other dealings in licences (see section 339 (4)),
caveats (see section 345 (3)),
withdrawals of caveats (see section 346 (2)),
consents to dealings given under section 350 (see section 350 (6)),
copies of court orders (see section 351).

heading.b: Form of register and document file

block.txt: The offshore mining register is to be kept in the form and manner determined by the Minister.
Without limiting subsection (1), the offshore mining register may be kept in the form of a computer record.
The document file is to be kept in the form and manner determined by the Minister.

heading.b: Correction of errors in the register

block.txt: Subject to subsection (4), the Minister may correct the offshore mining register if the Minister is satisfied that:
there is an omission of an entry from the register, or
an entry in the register should not have been made, or
there is an error or defect in an entry in the register.
A person may apply to the Minister for correction of the offshore mining register under subsection (1).
The application:
must be in writing, and
must specify the correction that is being requested.
If:
the Minister intends to correct the offshore mining register under subsection (1), and
the correction relates to a licence, and
the correction is not to be made in response to an application under subsection (2) by the licence holder,
the Minister must notify the holder that the Minister intends to correct the register.
The notice:
must be in writing, and
must specify the correction the Minister intends to make, and
must invite the holder to make submissions to the Minister about the proposed correction within the period specified in the notice.
The period specified under subsection (5) (c) is to be at least 14 days after the day on which the notice is given.
If a notice is given under subsection (4):
the Minister is not to correct the register until the period specified in the notice has ended, and
the Minister is to have regard to any submissions made by the licence holder before the end of that period in exercising the power under subsection (1) to correct the register.
A person may inspect the offshore mining register and the document file if the person pays the fee prescribed by the regulations.
The Minister must make the offshore mining register and the document file available for inspection at all convenient times.

heading.b: Matters to be entered in register

block.txt: If the provisional grant of a licence is properly accepted, the Minister must register:
the holder’s name, and
if there is more than one licence holder, the share in the licence held by each holder, and
a description of the licence area, including a map or map reference, and
the term of the licence, and
the date of the provisional grant of the licence, and
the date of registration of the licence, and
an address for the service of notices under this Act on the licence holder.
The address registered under subsection (1) (g) is to be the address specified by the licence holder by notice in writing to the Minister.

If the holder has not given a notice under subsection (2), the address to be registered under subsection (1) (g) is to be the address specified in the application that the holder made for the licence.
If the Minister registers a licence under subsection (1):
the licence holder must give the licence to the Minister, and
the Minister must endorse the date of registration on the licence.
The Minister may include in the register any other information about the holder or the terms and conditions of the licence that the Minister thinks is appropriate.
The Minister must keep a copy of the licence.
A licence is taken to be registered as soon as an entry complying with subsection (1) is made in the register.
If the Minister receives an application for the renewal of a licence, the Minister must register the fact.
If the provisional renewal of a licence is properly accepted, the Minister must register:
the renewal, and
the term of the renewal, and
the date of the provisional renewal, and
the date of registration of the renewal.
If the Minister registers the renewal of a licence under subsection (2):
the licence holder must give the licence to the Minister, and
the Minister must endorse on the licence:
the term of the renewal, and
the date of registration of the renewal.
If the Minister refuses to renew a licence, the Minister must register the refusal.
If the Minister receives an application for the extension of the term of an exploration licence, the Minister must register the fact.
If the Minister refuses to extend the term of an exploration licence, the Minister must register the refusal.
For extensions of the term of a licence see sections 94 to 98.
The grant of the extension of the term of an exploration licence is registered under section 337 (1).
If a licence expires because:
its term ends, or
a retention licence or mining licence is granted to the licence holder,
the Minister must register the expiry of the licence.
Cancellation is dealt with under section 337.
In subsection (1) (a), the reference to the term of a licence includes any period during which the licence is in force under section 90, 91, 92 or 93.
If the Minister registers the expiry of a licence under subsection (1):
the licence holder must give the licence to the Minister, and
the Minister must endorse the expiry and the date of the expiry on the licence.
The Minister must register:
the details of any document under this Act that varies, surrenders, cancels or otherwise affects a licence, and
the details of any document that varies or revokes a document referred to in paragraph (a).
The documents referred to in paragraph (a) are:
suspension of licence rights (see sections 48 (exploration licence), 135 (retention licence) and 195 (mining licence)),

amendment of licence conditions between provisional grant and registration (see sections 67 (exploration licence), 148 (retention licence), 211 (mining licence) and 280 (works licence))—these need to be registered at the same time as the grant is registered because if the conditions are amended between provisional grant and registration a replacement licence reflecting the change in conditions is not issued to the provisional holder,
extension of term (see sections 90, 95 and 97 (exploration licence)),
surrender of the whole or a part of a licence (see sections 99 and 127 (exploration licence), 158 and 187 (retention licence), 235 and 264 (mining licence) and 312 (works licence)),
voluntary surrender—special approval (see section 100 (exploration licence)),
mandatory reduction of licence area—special permission (see section 104 (exploration licence)),

amendment of licence conditions between provisional renewal and registration (see sections 111 (exploration licence), 170 (retention licence), 247 (mining licence) and 297 (works licence))—these need to be registered at the same time as the renewal because if the licence conditions are amended between provisional renewal and registration a replacement licence reflecting the changed conditions is not issued to the holder,
variation of conditions (see sections 120 (exploration licence), 179 (retention licence), 256 (mining licence) and 306 (works licence)),
exemption from or suspension of condition (see sections 121 (exploration licence), 180 (retention licence), 257 (mining licence) and 307 (works licence)),
cancellation (see sections 130 (exploration licence), 189 and 190 (retention licence), 265 (mining licence) and 313 (works licence)),
directions (see sections 387 and 392),
security requirements (see section 399),
approvals of transfers (see section 365).
Subsection (1) (a) applies to a document that suspends the rights of a holder of a licence.
Details of a document may be registered by registering a summary of the contents of the document.
The Minister must keep a document referred to in subsection (1), or a copy of the document.
A document referred to in subsection (1):
has no effect until it is registered, and
is taken to be registered as soon as an entry complying with subsection (1) is made in the register.
The Minister must register the transfer of a licence or a share in a licence if:
a party to the transfer lodges the instrument of transfer for registration, and
a party to the transfer lodges a copy of the instrument of transfer, and
the transfer has been approved by the Minister, and
the licence is lodged with the Minister for annotation under subsection (5), and
the fee prescribed by the regulations is paid, and
section 341 (caveats) does not prevent the registration of the transfer.
Paragraph (c): the Minister’s approval is endorsed on the transfer (see section 365 (3)).
The Minister must also register the date and time of registration of the transfer.

If an instrument purports to transfer a licence or a share in a licence, the Minister must register the instrument under this section without inquiring into or being concerned as to the legal effectiveness of the instrument.
If an instrument that transfers a licence or a share in a licence is registered, the Minister must register the name of the transferee as a licence holder.
If the Minister registers the transfer of a licence or a share in a licence, the Minister must annotate the licence to show the transferee as a licence holder.
The Minister must:
keep the copy of the transfer, and
return the transfer to the person who lodged it, and
return the annotated licence to the person who lodged it.
The registration of a document under this section does not give the document any greater effect than it would have had apart from this Act.
The Minister must register a document (other than a transfer of a licence or a share in a licence) that creates, transfers, affects or otherwise deals with an interest in a licence if:
a party to the dealing lodges the document for registration, and
a party to the dealing lodges a copy of the document, and
the fee prescribed by the regulations is paid, and
section 341 (caveats) does not prevent the registration of the dealing.
The Minister must also register the date and time of registration of the dealing.

If a document purports to create, transfer, affect or otherwise deal with an interest in a licence, the Minister is to register the document under this section without inquiring into or being concerned as to the legal effectiveness of the document.
The Minister must keep the copy of the document.
The Minister must return the document to the person who lodged it.
The registration of a document under this section does not give the document any greater effect than it would have had apart from this Act.
If:
the rights of a licence holder have devolved to a person by operation of law, and
the person applies to the Minister in writing to be registered as a licence holder, and
the licence is lodged with the Minister for annotation under subsection (3), and
the person pays the fee prescribed by the regulations, and
the Minister is satisfied that the applicant is entitled to those rights, and
section 341 (caveats) does not prevent the registration of the person as a licence holder,
the Minister must register the person as a licence holder.
If the Minister registers a person as a licence holder under subsection (1), the Minister must also register the date and time of registration.
If the Minister registers a person as a licence holder under subsection (1), the Minister must annotate the licence accordingly.
The Minister must return the annotated licence to the person who lodged it.
This section applies to 2 or more persons to whom rights have devolved in the same way as it applies to a single person to whom rights have devolved.
If a caveat is in force on a licence, the Minister must not register a dealing in the licence unless:
the Minister is not required to give the caveat holder notice of the particular dealing, or
the caveat holder consents to the registration of the dealing under section 350, or
a court of competent jurisdiction orders the Minister to register the dealing under section 338 or 339 despite the caveat.
For “dealing” see section 5.

Once the caveat holder has been given notice of the dealing, the caveat will lapse at the end of 30 days unless the caveat holder consents to the registration of the dealing or gets a court order extending the life of the caveat (see section 348).

The Minister may not be required to give the caveat holder notice of the dealing because the caveat holder is a party to the dealing or because the dealing falls outside the class of dealings that the caveat holder has specified under section 343 (2) (see section 349 (6)).
If a caveat is in force on a licence, the Minister must not register a person under section 340 as a licence holder unless:
the caveat holder consents to the registration under section 350, or
a court of competent jurisdiction orders the Minister to register the person under section 340 despite the caveat.
Once the caveat holder has been given notice, the caveat will lapse at the end of 30 days unless the caveat holder consents to the registration or gets a court order extending the life of the caveat.
A person who claims a legal or equitable interest in or affecting a licence may lodge with the Minister a caveat on the licence.
A person may claim a legal or equitable interest in or affecting a licence even if the interest claimed arises under a document that has not been registered under section 338 or 339.
A caveat must:
be in accordance with the form approved by the Minister, and
set out:
the full name and address of the person claiming the interest, and
details of the interest claimed, and
be signed by the person claiming the interest, and
specify an address for service of notices within the State.
A caveat may specify the particular dealings that the caveat holder wants to be given notice of under section 349.
The person lodging a caveat must pay the caveat fee determined from time to time by the Minister with the concurrence of the Treasurer.
If:
a caveat is lodged for registration, and
the caveat complies with section 343, and
the person lodging the caveat pays the fee required by section 344,
the Minister must, subject to subsection (4), register the caveat.
The Minister must register the date and time of lodgment.
The Minister must keep the original of the caveat and endorse on it the date and time of lodgment.
Subsection (1) does not apply if:
the Supreme Court has made an order under section 351 (2), and
the order requires the Court’s consent to the registration of the caveat, and
the Court has not consented to the registration of the caveat.
A caveat holder may withdraw the caveat at any time by lodging a written withdrawal with the Minister.
The Minister must:
register details of the withdrawal, and
endorse details of the withdrawal on the original of the caveat, and
keep the original of the withdrawal.
A withdrawal of a caveat must:
be in accordance with the approved form, and
give details of the caveat, and
be signed by the caveat holder.
A caveat that is registered is taken to have had effect from the time at which it is lodged with the Minister.
A caveat on a licence ceases to have effect if:
the Supreme Court makes an order for the removal of the caveat under section 351, or
the caveat is withdrawn under section 346, or
the caveat holder is given notice under section 349 (1), (2) or (3) and 30 days have passed since the caveat holder was given the notice.
Subsection (2) (c) does not apply if, before the end of the 30 days, the caveat holder consents to the registration of the dealing or to the registration under section 340.
Subsection (2) (c) does not apply if, before the end of the 30 days:
the Supreme Court makes an order extending the period.
If a court makes an order under section 351 (1) (c), the caveat ceases to have effect at the end of the extended period.
Subsection (5) does not apply if, before the end of the extended period, the caveat holder consents to the registration of the dealing under section 350 or to the registration under section 340.
If:
a transfer of a licence or a share in a licence is lodged with the Minister under section 338, and
a caveat is in force on the licence,
the Minister must, subject to subsection (6), notify the caveat holder that the transfer has been lodged for registration.
If:
a dealing in a licence (other than a transfer of the licence or a share in the licence) is lodged with the Minister under section 339, and
a caveat is in force on the licence,
the Minister must, subject to subsection (6), notify the caveat holder that the dealing has been lodged for registration.
If:
a person applies to the Minister under section 340 to be registered as a licence holder, and
a caveat is in force on the licence,
the Minister must notify the caveat holder that the application has been made.
If:
a licence holder surrenders the licence or surrenders a block or some of the blocks covered by the licence, and
a caveat is in force on the licence,
the Minister must notify the caveat holder of the surrender.
Notification under subsection (1), (2), (3) or (4) must be by certified mail.
Notice is not to be given under subsection (1) or (2) if:
the caveat holder is a party to the transfer or dealing concerned, or
the caveat holder has specified the class of dealings the caveat holder wants to receive notice of (see section 343 (2)) and the transfer or dealing falls outside that class.

heading.b: Caveat holder may consent to registration

block.txt: If a caveat holder is given notice under section 349 (1), the caveat holder may consent to the registration of the transfer.
If a caveat holder is given notice under section 349 (2), the caveat holder may consent to the registration of the dealing.
If a caveat holder is given notice under section 349 (3), the caveat holder may consent to the registration of the person as a licence holder.
A consent under this section must be in writing and must be lodged with the Minister.
A consent under this section is only effective if it is given within 30 days after the day on which the caveat holder receives the notice concerned.
The Minister must:
register details of the consent, and
endorse details of the consent on the original of the caveat, and
keep the original of the consent.

heading.b: Orders that can be made by a court in relation to caveats

block.txt: The Supreme Court may:
order the removal of a caveat from a licence, or
order the Minister to register a dealing despite a caveat, or
extend the period provided for by section 348 (2) (c).
If:
the Supreme Court makes an order under subsection (1) (a) or (b) in relation to the licence, and
the Court is satisfied that caveats are being used vexatiously to delay the registration of a document,
the Court may also make an order that the Minister is not to register any caveats in respect of the licence unless the Court has consented to the registration.
An order under subsection (2) may be for an indefinite period or for a specified period.
An order under subsection (2) may provide that the Court’s consent is not required in any specified case or class of case.
If an application is made to the Court for an order under subsection (2), the Minister becomes a party to the proceedings.
If the Court makes an order under this section, the Minister must:
register details of the order, and
keep a copy of the order.
The Minister, with the concurrence of the Treasurer, is to determine from time to time the fees payable under this Act for registration of any document or fact.
Duty under the Stamp Duties Act 1920 or the Duties Act 1997 is not chargeable:
on a licence, or
on any instrument that creates, transfers, affects or otherwise deals with an interest in a licence.
This section applies to:
the Minister, and
a delegate of the Minister, and
a person acting under the direction or authority of the Minister or a delegate of the Minister.
the act or matter is done or omitted to be done in the exercise or purported exercise of a power or authority given by this Part, and
the act or matter is done or omitted to be done in good faith.

heading.b: Application to Supreme Court for correction of register

block.txt: The Supreme Court, on the application of a person aggrieved by:
the omission of an entry from the offshore mining register, or
an entry wrongly existing in the register, or
an error or defect in an entry in the register,
may make any order it thinks appropriate directing correction of the register.
In any proceedings under subsection (1), the Supreme Court may decide any necessary or expedient question concerning the rectification of the register.
A copy of a Supreme Court order may be served on the Minister.
In any proceedings under subsection (1):
the Minister may appear, or
if the Supreme Court so directs, the Minister must appear.
If the Minister receives a copy of an order under subsection (3), the Minister must amend the register so that the register accords with the order.
If a person is dissatisfied with a determination by the Minister under section 352, the person may appeal to the Supreme Court against the determination.
Written notice of an appeal under subsection (1) must be given to the Minister.
In any proceedings under this section:
the Minister may appear, or
if the Supreme Court so directs, the Minister must appear.
On hearing an appeal under subsection (1), the Supreme Court may affirm, revoke or amend the determination of the Minister.
See note 2 to section 3 (1).
The offshore mining register is admissible in proceedings as evidence of the matters registered in it.
If the register is kept by the use of a computer, the Minister may issue a document containing the details of a matter taken from the register.
The document issued under subsection (2) is admissible in proceedings as evidence of the matter.
The Minister may give a person a certified copy of, or extract from, the register if the person pays the fee prescribed by the regulations.
The certified copy is admissible in proceedings without any further proof of, or the production of, the original.

heading.b: Certified copy of document on document file

block.txt: The Minister may give a person a certified copy of a document that is kept on the document file if the person pays the fee prescribed by the regulations.
The certified copy is admissible in proceedings without any further proof of, or the production of, the original.
The Minister may give a person a signed certificate that:
a thing required or allowed by this Part has been done, or
a thing required or allowed by this Part has not been done,
if the person pays the fee prescribed by the regulations.
The certificate is admissible in proceedings as evidence of the facts stated in the certificate.

heading.b: Dealings in licences to be in writing and registered
Dealings in licences to be in writing

block.txt: An interest in a licence may be created, transferred, affected or otherwise dealt with only by a written document.
A transfer must be in writing because it is a dealing.
Subsection (1) does not apply to the rights of a licence holder that devolve to a person by operation of law.
Rights might devolve to a person, for example, by operation of the laws relating to intestacy or bankruptcy.
For the registration of rights that devolve to a person by operation of law see section 340.

heading.b: Dealings in interests in licences not effective until registered

block.txt: A document that creates, transfers, affects or otherwise deals with an interest in a licence has no effect until it is registered under Part 3.1.
A transfer is a dealing and does not take effect until registered.
Transfers are registered under section 338 and other dealings under section 339.
The transfer of a licence is not to be registered under section 338 unless it has been approved by the Minister.
For “transfer” of a licence see section 7 (1).
A transfer is a dealing and under section 361 does not take effect until registered.
The transfer of a share in a licence is not to be registered under section 338 unless it has been approved by the Minister.
For “transfer” in a share of a licence see section 7 (2) and (3).
A transfer is a dealing and under section 361 does not take effect until registered.
A person may apply to the Minister for approval of the transfer.
The application must be in writing.
The application must be accompanied by:
the transfer document (duly signed or executed), and
a copy of the transfer document, and
if a caveat holder has consented to the registration of the transfer under section 350 (1), a copy of the consent.
The application may include a statement of any matter that the applicant wants the Minister to take into account in deciding whether to approve the transfer.
Without limiting subsection (4), the application may include a statement about:
the technical qualifications of a party to the transfer, or
the technical qualifications of the employees of a party to the transfer, or
the technical advice available to a party to the transfer, or
the financial resources of a party to the transfer.
The application must be accompanied by the appropriate application fee.

heading.b: Minister may ask for further information

block.txt: If:
an application is made under section 363 for approval of a transfer, and
the Minister has reason to believe that a person possesses or controls a document that relates to:
the transfer document, or
the transfer transaction, or
the application for approval of the transfer,
the Minister may ask the person:
to give the document to the Minister, or
to make the document available for inspection by or on behalf of the Minister.
The request under subsection (1) must be made by giving to the person a written notice containing the request.
A person must not fail to comply with a request under subsection (1) without reasonable excuse.
Maximum penalty: $5 000.

heading.b: Minister’s response to application for approval

block.txt: If an application is made under section 363, the Minister may:
approve the transfer, or
refuse to approve the transfer.
The Minister may, under subsection (1) (a), approve the transfer on conditions that the Minister considers necessary or desirable in the public interest.
If the Minister approves the transfer, the Minister must endorse on:
the transfer document, and
a copy of the transfer document,
a record of the approval.
A record of the approval will also be entered in the offshore mining register (see section 338 (1)).
This section applies to:
the Minister, and
a delegate of the Minister, and
a person acting under the direction or authority of the Minister or a delegate of the Minister.
the act or matter is done or omitted to be done in the exercise or purported exercise of a power or authority given by this Part, and
the act or matter is done or omitted to be done in good faith.

heading.b: Minister may ask person for information

block.txt: The Minister may ask a person to give the Minister information if:
the information is relevant to the operation of this Act, and
the Minister has reasonable grounds for believing that the person is able to give the information.
The person must comply with the request (see section 372).
The Minister may ask the person to give the information to:
the Minister, or
an inspector nominated by the Minister.
The request must:
be made by written notice given to the person, and
specify the person to whom the information is to be given, and
specify the period within which the information is to be given.
The information must be given:
in writing, and
before the end of the period specified in the request.
The document containing the information must be signed by:
if the information is given by a body corporate, an authorised officer of the body corporate, or
if the information is provided by an individual, the individual.

heading.b: Power to ask person to appear

block.txt: If the Minister has reasonable grounds for believing that a person is able to give information that is relevant to the operation of this Act, the Minister may ask the person to appear personally to:
give the information, and
answer questions about the activity to which the information relates.
The person must comply with the request (see section 372).
The Minister may ask a person to appear before:
the Minister, or
an inspector nominated by the Minister.
The request must:
be made by written notice given to the person, and
specify the activity about which the information is sought or questions will be asked, and
specify the address at which the person is to attend, and
specify the day on which and the time at which the person is to attend, and
indicate whether the appearance is to be before the Minister or before a nominated inspector.

heading.b: Power to examine on oath or affirmation

block.txt: Where, following a notice under section 368, a person appears before the Minister or a nominated inspector, the Minister or the inspector may:
administer an oath or affirmation to the person, and
request the person to answer any question that comes within the terms of the notice.
The oath or affirmation to be administered is an oath or affirmation that the person will truthfully answer the questions put by the Minister or the inspector.
The Minister may ask a person to produce a document if:
the document is relevant to the operation of this Act, and
the Minister has reasonable grounds for believing that the person is able to produce the document.
The person must comply with the request (see section 372).
The Minister may ask the person to produce the document to:
the Minister, or
an inspector nominated by the Minister.
The request:
must be made by written notice given to the person, and
must specify the person to whom, and the address at which, the document is to be produced, and
must specify:
the period within which the document is to be produced, or
the day on which and the time at which the document is to be produced, and
may specify whether the original or a copy of the document is to be produced.
The regulations may provide for the manner in which the Minister is to deal with the document.
Without limiting subsection (4), the regulations may authorise the Minister or inspector to take a copy of the document.
The Minister may ask a person to produce a sample taken from the seabed or subsoil in coastal waters if:
the sample is relevant to the operation of this Act, and
the Minister has reasonable grounds for believing that the person is able to produce the sample.
The person must comply with the request (see section 372).
The Minister may ask the person to give the sample to:
the Minister, or
an inspector nominated by the Minister.
The request:
must be made by written notice given to the person, and
must specify the person to whom, and the address at which, the sample is to be given, and
must specify:
the period within which the sample is to be given, or
the day on which and the time at which the sample is to be given.
The regulations may provide for the manner in which the Minister or inspector is to deal with the sample.
Without limiting subsection (4), the regulations may authorise the Minister or inspector to test or analyse the sample.

heading.b: Obligation to comply with request under section 367, 368, 369, 370 or 371

block.txt: A person must not, without reasonable excuse, fail to comply with a request under section 367, 368, 369, 370 or 371.
Maximum penalty: $10 000.
A person is not excused from complying with the request on the ground that complying with the request might tend to incriminate the person or make the person liable to a penalty.
Section 373 provides immunity for the response to the request.
A person must not give false or misleading information:
in response to a request under section 367, 368, 370 or 371, or
in response to a question asked under section 369 (1).
Maximum penalty: $10 000.

heading.b: Immunity from use of information etc given in response to request under section 367, 368, 369, 370 or 371

block.txt: Where a person gives the Minister information in response to a request under section 367 or 368, or to a question under section 369 (1), the following are not admissible in evidence against the person in any proceedings:
the document containing the information given in response to the request, or
the answer to the question, or
any information, document or thing obtained as a direct or indirect consequence of the giving of the information or answer.
If a person produces a document in response to a request under section 370, the following are not admissible in evidence against the person in any proceedings:
the document,
the fact of the production of the document by the person,
any information, document or thing obtained as a direct or indirect consequence of the production of the document.
If a person produces a sample in response to a request under section 371, the following are not admissible in evidence against the person in any proceedings:
the sample,
the fact of the production of the sample by the person,
any information, document or thing obtained as a direct or indirect consequence of the production of the sample.
The immunity provided by subsections (1), (2) and (3) does not apply to proceedings for an offence against section 372 (3).

heading.b: Restrictions on release of confidential material

block.txt: Subject to sections 375 and 376, if the Minister holds confidential information:
the Minister, and
a Commonwealth or State Minister who is given the information under section 375, and
a person acting on behalf of the Minister or of a Minister referred to in paragraph (b), and
a person who is given the information under section 375 (3),
must not:
publish the information, or
make the information available to a person.
Maximum penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years.
Subject to section 375, if the Minister holds a confidential sample:
the Minister, and
a Commonwealth or State Minister who is given access to the sample under section 375, and
a person acting on behalf of the Minister or of a Minister referred to in paragraph (b), and
a person who is given access to the sample under section 375 (4),
must not:
allow a person to inspect the sample, or
publish information about the sample.
Maximum penalty: Imprisonment for 2 years.

heading.b: Circumstances in which confidential material may be released

block.txt: If:
a licence holder gives confidential information to the Minister, and
the holder:
makes the information publicly available, or
consents in writing to the information being made publicly available,
the Minister, or another State Minister or a Commonwealth Minister who is given access to the information, may make the information available to any person.
If:
a licence holder gives a confidential sample to the Minister, and
the holder:
publishes details of the sample, or
consents in writing to the details being made publicly available, or
consents in writing to the sample being made available for public inspection,
the Minister, or another State Minister or a Commonwealth Minister who is given access to the sample, may:
make details of the sample available to any person, or
allow any person to inspect the sample.
For “confidential information” and “confidential sample” see sections 27 and 28.
Confidential information may be made available to a person if the information is made available for the purposes of the administration of this Act.
A person may be given access to a confidential sample if the access is given for the purposes of the administration of this Act.

heading.b: Certain reports to be made available

block.txt: If:
in order to comply with:
the regulations, or
a direction under section 387 or 392, or
a licence condition,
a licence holder gives the Minister a report, and
the report relates to blocks that are no longer covered by the licence or by a successor licence to the licence, and
another person requests the Minister to make the report available to the person,
the Minister must make the report available to the person on payment of such fee as is determined by the Minister, with the concurrence of the Treasurer.
For the purposes of this Act, a compliance inspection is an inspection carried out to determine whether:
a licence holder, a special purpose consent holder or an associate has complied with or is complying with:
this Act or the regulations, or
the licence or consent conditions, or
a direction under section 387 or 392, or
a person is exploring for or recovering minerals in breach of section 38.
An inspector may carry out a compliance inspection under:
section 379 (inspection of licence-related premises etc without a warrant),
section 380 (inspection of other premises etc with consent of the occupier),
section 381 (inspection of premises etc with a warrant).

heading.b: Powers exercisable in course of inspection

block.txt: If an inspector may carry out a compliance inspection, the inspector may do anything that is reasonable and necessary to carry out the inspection.
Without limiting subsection (1), the inspector may:
examine things that are being used for exploration or mining purposes and things that appear to the inspector to be intended to be used for those purposes, and
test equipment (for example, by operating it), and
examine, and copy, documents, and
remove documents, and
take photographs and videotapes, and
examine, and take samples from the seabed or subsoil, and
enter or go onto any land, building or structure, and
enter or board any vehicle, vessel or aircraft.
If the compliance inspection is being carried out under a warrant under section 382, subsection (2) has effect subject to the restrictions that are specified in the warrant.

Subject to subsections (5) and (6), if an inspector removes a document under subsection (2) (d), the inspector may retain the document for as long as is necessary to determine whether the licence holder, the consent holder or the associate has complied with or is complying with:
this Act and the regulations, or
the licence or consent conditions, or
a direction under section 387 or 392.
Subject to subsection (6), the inspector must not retain the document for more than 60 days.
If:
proceedings for an offence against a provision of this Act or the regulations are commenced within that period of 60 days, and
the document may afford evidence of the commission of the offence,
the inspector may retain the document until the proceedings are completed.
For the purposes of subsection (6), the proceedings for an offence are taken to include any appeal to a court in relation to those proceedings.

While an inspector is retaining the document under subsection (4), the inspector must allow a person to inspect the document if the person would have a right to inspect the document if it were not in the inspector’s possession.

heading.b: Inspection of licence-related premises etc without warrant

block.txt: Subject to subsections (2), (3) and (4), an inspector may, without a warrant, carry out a compliance inspection of:
licence-related land, or
a licence-related building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft,
if the inspection is reasonably necessary.
An inspection under subsection (1) must be made at a reasonable time.
An inspector may not enter premises under subsection (1) if:
the premises are a residence, and
the occupier has not consented to the entry.
An inspector may not carry out a compliance inspection under subsection (1) if:
the person occupying or in charge of the land, building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft concerned asks the inspector to produce the inspector’s identity card for inspection by the person, and
the inspector does not comply with the person’s request.
For the purposes of this section, land or a building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft is licence-related if:
it is used in connection with activities carried out under a licence or special purpose consent, or
records about activities of that kind are kept there.

heading.b: Inspection of other premises etc with occupier’s consent

block.txt: An inspector may carry out a compliance inspection of land or a building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft with the consent of the person who occupies or is in charge of the land, building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft.

heading.b: Inspection of other premises etc with warrant

block.txt: An inspector may carry out a compliance inspection in accordance with a warrant issued under section 382.

An inspector may apply to an authorised officer (within the meaning of the Law Enforcement (Powers and Responsibilities) Act 2002) for a warrant to carry out a compliance inspection of land or of a building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft.
The application must be supported by a statement on oath or affirmation that sets out the grounds on which the inspector is applying for the warrant.
If the authorised officer is satisfied that the compliance inspection is reasonably necessary, the authorised officer may issue a warrant to the inspector to carry out the inspection.
The warrant must state:
the name of the inspector, and
whether the inspection may be carried out at any time or only during specified hours of the day, and
the day on which the warrant ceases to have effect, and
the purposes for which the warrant is issued.
The day specified under subsection (4) (c) is not to be more than 7 days after the day on which the warrant is issued.
The purposes specified under subsection (4) (d) must include the identification of:
the land, building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft to be inspected, and
any equipment that the inspector may test, and
any documents that the inspector may examine and copy, and
any cores or cuttings from the seabed or subsoil that the inspector may examine and take samples of.

heading.b: Further provisions as to exercise of powers under warrant

block.txt: If a warrant for a compliance inspection is issued to an inspector under section 382, the warrant authorises the inspector to carry out the inspection:
with such assistance as is reasonable and necessary, and
by such force as is reasonable and necessary.
An inspector may not carry out a compliance inspection under a warrant if:
the person occupying or in charge of the land, building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft concerned asks the inspector to produce the inspector’s identity card for inspection by the person, and
the inspector does not comply with the person’s request.

If an inspector carries out a compliance inspection of land or of a building, structure, vehicle, vessel or aircraft under section 379 or 381, the person who occupies or is in charge of it must provide the inspector with the facilities and assistance that the inspector reasonably requires for carrying out the inspection.
Maximum penalty: $5 000.

heading.b: Directions by Minister must be obeyed

block.txt: A person must comply with a direction under section 387 or 392.
Maximum penalty: $10 000.
A person must comply with a supplementary direction given under section 391 (2).
Maximum penalty: $5 000.
The Minister may give a direction under section 387 or 392 if it is necessary or convenient to do so to carry out or give effect to this Act or the regulations.
Without limiting subsection (1), directions may be given in relation to:
the control of offshore exploration or mining activities, and
the conservation and protection of the mineral resources in coastal waters, and
the remedying of:
damage caused to the seabed or subsoil in coastal waters by offshore exploration or mining activities, or
damage caused by the escape of substances as a result of offshore exploration or mining activities, and
the protection of the environment, and
the keeping of records and samples, and
the giving of records and samples to the Minister for inspection, and
the making of returns.
For “offshore exploration or mining activities” see section 5.
For the purposes of subsection (2), the control of offshore exploration or mining activities extends to the control of:
the construction, maintenance and operation of installations used in or for use in exploration or mining activities in coastal waters, and
the flow or discharge of fluids arising from exploration or mining activities in coastal waters, and
the safety, health and welfare of persons working in offshore exploration or mining activities, and
the maintenance of structures, equipment and property used in or for use in offshore exploration or mining activities.
For “offshore exploration or mining activities” see section 5.
Subject to subsections (2), (3) and (4), the Minister may direct a licence holder or special purpose consent holder to do or not to do the thing specified in the direction.
The direction must be in writing and is given by serving it on the holder.
The Minister must not give a direction of a permanent or standing nature except after consultation with the responsible Commonwealth Minister.
A failure to comply with subsection (3) does not affect the validity of the direction concerned.

heading.b: Direction may incorporate material in another document

block.txt: A direction under section 387 may apply, adopt or incorporate a code of practice or a standard that is contained in another document.
The application, adoption or incorporation of the other document may be made with or without modification.
The other document may be one issued outside Australia.
The direction may apply, adopt or modify the other document:
as in force at the time when the direction is given, or
as in force from time to time.

If a direction applies, adopts or incorporates material in another document, a copy of the document must be attached to the direction when it is given to the licence holder or special purpose consent holder.
Without limiting section 387, a direction under that section may:
prohibit absolutely the doing of a thing, or
prohibit the doing of a thing unless a person’s consent or approval is obtained.
A direction under section 387 to a licence holder or special purpose consent holder may extend to an associate specified in the direction.
An associate may be specified by name or by class.
The direction may provide that only particular obligations specified in the direction extend to a particular associate.

heading.b: Holder to give notice of direction to associates

block.txt: If a direction under section 387 extends to an associate, the licence holder or special purpose consent holder must either:
give a copy of the direction to the associate, or
display a copy of the direction at a place that the associate goes to in the course of carrying out activities under the licence or consent.
Maximum penalty: $5 000.

The Minister may give the licence holder or special purpose consent holder a supplementary direction that specifies the manner in which, or the places at which, copies of a direction are to be displayed under subsection (1) (b).
A supplementary direction is to have effect as if it were part of the original direction.

heading.b: Power to give directions after licence etc ends

block.txt: If a person is bound by an obligation because of section 131, 191, 266 or 314, the Minister may direct the person to do a thing or not to do a thing specified in the direction.
A direction may be given only for the following purposes:
to ensure that the obligation is complied with,
a purpose that is incidental to the purpose in paragraph (a).
Sections 131, 191, 266 and 314 provide for undischarged obligations to continue to bind a former licence holder or associate after the licence ends.
A direction must be in writing and is given by serving it on the person bound by the obligation.

heading.b: Effect of directions on other instruments

block.txt: A later direction under section 387 or 392 overrides an earlier direction if they are inconsistent.
A direction has effect despite anything in:
the regulations, or
a licence condition that relates to safety or environmental matters.

heading.b: Minister may specify time for compliance

block.txt: If the Minister gives a direction under section 387 or 392 to a person, the Minister may:
specify in the direction a time for compliance with the direction, or
give the person a supplementary direction specifying a time for compliance with the direction.
A supplementary direction is to have effect as if it were part of the original direction.

heading.b: Minister may take action if holder fails to comply

block.txt: The Minister may do all or any of the things required by a direction under section 387 or 392 if:
the time for compliance specified under section 394 has ended, and
the person to whom the direction was given or to whom it extended has not complied with the direction.
If the direction required consultation under section 387 (3), the Minister must not take action under subsection (1) without similar consultation.

heading.b: Costs incurred by Minister in taking action under section 395

block.txt: If:
the Minister takes action under section 395 in relation to a direction under section 387 given to a licence holder or special purpose consent holder, and
the direction does not extend to an associate of the holder,
the costs and expenses incurred by the Minister in taking that action are a debt due to the State by the holder.
If:
a direction under section 387 specifies that a particular associate of a licence holder or special purpose consent holder is subject to a particular obligation, and
the Minister takes action under section 395 in relation to that obligation,
the costs and expenses incurred by the Minister in taking that action are a debt due to the State by the holder and the associate.
The associate and the holder are jointly and severally liable to pay the debt arising under subsection (2).
A debt under this section is recoverable in a court of competent jurisdiction.

heading.b: Defences to actions to recover debts

block.txt: the holder or associate produces evidence that the holder or associate took all reasonable steps to comply with the direction, and
the evidence is not rebutted.
It is a defence to an action to recover the debt from the associate if:
the associate produces evidence that the associate did not know of, and could not reasonably be expected to know of, the existence of the direction, and
the evidence is not rebutted.
A person may be required to lodge a security with the Minister under:
section 399 (security as prerequisite for proper acceptance of provisional grant or provisional renewal), or
section 118 (exploration licence conditions), 177 (retention licence conditions), 254 (mining licence conditions) or 304 (works licence conditions).
Securities are required as a way of ensuring compliance with this Act and with licence conditions.
Securities may only be used for the purposes laid down in section 400.

heading.b: Determination of requirement to lodge security

block.txt: The Minister may determine that a person who has been provisionally granted a licence must lodge a security with the Minister.
The provisional holder will be given notice of the determination under section 66 or 83 (exploration licence), 147 (retention licence), 210 or 227 (mining licence) or 279 (works licence).

If the provisional holder does not lodge the security within a particular time provided for in this Act, the provisional grant will lapse (see section 72 or 86 (exploration licence), 153 (retention licence), 216 or 230 (mining licence) or 285 (works licence)).
If the Minister provisionally renews a licence, the Minister may determine that the licence holder must lodge a security with the Minister.
The licence holder will be given notice of the determination under section 110 (exploration licence), 169 (retention licence), 246 (mining licence) or 296 (works licence).

If the holder does not lodge the security within a particular time provided for in this Act, the provisional renewal will lapse (see section 116 (exploration licence), 175 (retention licence), 252 (mining licence) or 302 (works licence)).
A determination under subsection (1) or (2) must specify:
the amount of the security required, and
the kind of security required, and
the manner and form in which the security is to be lodged.
Without limiting subsections (1) and (2), a determination may require the lodgment of a security in the form of a guarantee and if a guarantee is required the determination may specify:
the kind of person who is to give the guarantee, and
the terms of the guarantee.
The determination is to be in writing.

If a person is provisionally granted a licence over a tender block, the amount determined as a security under subsection (1) is to be the amount of security referred to in the tender block licence notice.
For the contents of a tender block licence notice see sections 75 and 219.
If:
a person is or was a licence holder, and
the person has lodged a security with the Minister,
the Minister may use the security to discharge the person’s obligations arising from a failure to comply with:
this Act or the regulations, or
the licence conditions, or
a direction under section 387 or 392.
Without limiting subsection (1), the holder’s financial obligations include the obligation to pay a penalty imposed under the licence conditions.
Subject to subsection (1), the Minister is to deal with a security in accordance with the regulations.

heading.b: Removal of property from coastal waters

block.txt: The regulations may provide for:
the removal from coastal waters of property that:
has been brought into coastal waters for use in offshore exploration or mining activities, and
is not being used and is not intended to be used in exploration or mining activities in accordance with a licence, and
the disposal by the Minister of property removed under regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (a), and
the recovery of costs and expenses incurred by the Minister or another person in removing or disposing of property in accordance with regulations made for the purposes of paragraphs (a) and (b).
For “offshore exploration or mining activities” see section 5.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) (a) may provide for removal by the Minister or by someone else.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) (c) may provide for the recovery of costs by way of deduction from the proceeds of the disposal.
Subject to the regulations, no action lies in respect of the removal or disposal of property in accordance with the regulations.
In this section:
property includes a structure or equipment.
The regulations may provide for:
the rehabilitation of an area in coastal waters that has been damaged or affected by offshore exploration or mining activities of a licence holder, and
the recovery of costs and expenses incurred by the Minister in rehabilitating an area under regulations made for the purposes of paragraph (a).
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) (a) may provide for the rehabilitation to be carried out by the Minister or someone else.
Regulations made for the purposes of subsection (1) (b) may provide for the recovery of costs and expenses by way of deduction from the licence holder’s security.

heading.b: Declaration of safety zone around a structure or equipment

block.txt: The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, establish a safety zone around a structure or equipment in coastal waters.
A safety zone may only be established for the purpose of protecting the structure or equipment.
The safety zone may extend not more than 500 metres from the outer edge of the structure or equipment.
The order may apply to:
all vessels, or
all vessels except those specified in the order.

heading.b: Effect of declaration of safety zone

block.txt: If a safety zone is established by order under section 403, a vessel to which the order applies is not to enter or remain in the safety zone without the written consent of the Minister.
If a consent is given under subsection (1) on conditions, a vessel to which the consent applies is to enter or remain in the safety zone only in accordance with the conditions.

The owner of a vessel and the person in command or in charge of a vessel are each guilty of an indictable offence if the vessel enters or remains in a safety zone in contravention of subsection (1) or (2).
Maximum penalty: imprisonment for 5 years.
The Local Court may hear and determine proceedings for an offence against subsection (3) if the court is satisfied that it is appropriate to do so, and the defendant and the prosecutor consent.
Where, in accordance with subsection (3), the Local Court convicts a person of the offence, the person is liable to a fine of $10 000 or imprisonment for 2 years, or both.
It is a defence to a prosecution of a person for an offence against subsection (3) if the person satisfies the court that:
an unforeseen emergency made it necessary for the vessel to enter or remain in the safety zone to attempt to secure the safety of:
a human life, or
the vessel, or
another vessel, or
a well, pipeline, structure or equipment, or
the vessel entered or remained in the safety zone in circumstances beyond the control of the person who was in command or in charge of the vessel (for example, adverse weather).
It is a defence to a prosecution of the owner of a vessel for an offence against subsection (3) if the owner satisfies the court that the owner:
did not aid, abet, counsel or procure the vessel’s entering or remaining in the safety zone, and
was not in any way, directly or indirectly, knowingly concerned in, or party to, the vessel’s entering or remaining in the safety zone.
See note 2 to section 3 (1).
The Minister may appoint a person to be an inspector for the purposes of this Act and the regulations.
Inspectors have powers under sections 367, 368, 369, 370, 371, 378, 379, 380 and 381.
The appointment must be in writing.
The Minister must issue an inspector with an identity card.
The card must:
contain a recent photograph of the inspector, and
be in the form approved by the Minister.

A person who stops being an inspector must, as soon as is practicable, return the person’s identity card to the Minister or to an official specified by the Minister in a written notice given to the person.
A person must not contravene subsection (1) without reasonable excuse.
Maximum penalty: $100.
In this Division:
year, in relation to the period when a licence is in force, means:
the period of 12 months commencing on (and including) the day on which the provisional grant of the licence is properly accepted, or
a period of 12 months commencing on (and including) an anniversary of that day, or
a period of less than 12 months that:
commences on (and includes):
the day on which the provisional grant of the licence is properly accepted, or
an anniversary of that day, and
ends on the expiry of the licence.
A licence holder must pay a fee to the Minister for each year during which the licence is in force.
The amount of the fee for each kind of licence is to be as determined from time to time by the Minister, with the concurrence of the Treasurer, for that kind of licence.
If the licence has 2 or more holders, the holders are jointly and severally liable to pay the fee.
See note 2 to section 3 (1).
The fee for a year becomes payable one month after the day on which the year begins.
In this Division:
royalty period, in relation to a mining licence, means:
the period from (and including) the day on which the licence takes effect to (and including) the next 30 June or 31 December whichever is the earlier, and
each period of 6 months after that period.
A person who is or has been a mining licence holder must pay to the State a royalty for all minerals recovered by the holder under the licence.
The regulations may prescribe rates of royalty for the purposes of this Division.
Without limiting subsection (1), the rates of royalty prescribed under that subsection may include a rate that is related to the landed value, or to the quantity, of the mineral.
A rate of royalty prescribed under subsection (1) applies in relation to any mineral of the relevant kind recovered under a mining licence during the period when the rate is in force.

heading.b: Reduction of royalty in certain cases

block.txt: The Minister may determine a rate of royalty that is lower than the rate prescribed under section 430 for:
a particular kind of mineral, or
all minerals recovered under a particular mining licence.
A determination is to be made by instrument in writing and is to specify the period for which the lower rate is to be in force.
A determination may only be made under this section if the Minister is satisfied that recovery of the kind of mineral to which it applies would be uneconomic at the rate prescribed under section 430.
A determination under this section takes effect on the day on which the instrument of determination is published in the Gazette.
The Chief Commissioner is to be advised of any determination made under this section.
For the purposes of this Division, the landed value of a mineral is:
an amount agreed between the mining licence holder and the Minister, or
if there is no agreement within such period as the Minister allows, an amount determined by the Minister by instrument in writing.

A certificate that is signed by the Minister and that states that, on a specified date, the Minister made a determination under subsection (1) (b) is admissible in evidence in any proceedings and is evidence of the fact or facts so certified.
The Chief Commissioner may request a certificate under this section and a certificate is to be provided in accordance with that request.
For the purposes of this Division, the quantity of any mineral recovered by a mining licence holder during a royalty period is:
the quantity agreed between the holder and the Minister, or
if there is no agreement within such period as the Minister allows, the quantity determined by the Minister by instrument in writing.

A certificate that is signed by the Minister and that states that, on a specified date, the Minister made a determination under subsection (1) (b) is admissible in evidence in any proceedings and is evidence of the fact or facts so certified.
The Chief Commissioner may request a certificate under this section and a certificate is to be provided in accordance with that request.
Royalty for any mineral recovered during a royalty period is payable within one month after the last day of that royalty period.
A failure to pay the royalty within one month after the last day of that royalty period is a tax default for the purposes of the Taxation Administration Act 1996.
If a tax default occurs, interest and penalty tax may be charged under the Taxation Administration Act 1996.
A tax default does not occur in respect of an amount of royalty payable until the expiration of 7 days after:
the landed value of the mineral has been agreed or determined under section 432, where the rate of royalty is related to the landed value of the mineral, or
the quantity of the mineral has been agreed or determined under section 433, where the rate of royalty is related to the quantity of the mineral recovered.

heading.b: State to pay 40% of royalties to Commonwealth

block.txt: The State is to pay to the Commonwealth 40% of royalties received under this Division.
Payments under subsection (1) are to be made not later than the end of the month that follows the month in which the royalties were received.
In this section:
royalty includes any interest or penalty tax for late payment of royalty.
A person who is required to pay royalty under this Act is required to lodge with the Chief Commissioner a return relating to each royalty period.
The return is to be lodged with the Chief Commissioner within one month after the last day of that royalty period.
The Chief Commissioner is to give a copy to the Minister of each return lodged with the Chief Commissioner.
The Minister may give directions to the Chief Commissioner as to the information that is to be included in the form of return approved under the Taxation Administration Act 1996.
The Taxation Administration Act 1996 requires a return to be in a form approved by the Chief Commissioner.

The Minister, or a person engaged in the administration of this Act, may disclose royalty information obtained from a tax officer under this Act or the Taxation Administration Act 1996 in connection with the administration or execution of this Act.
This section applies despite section 84 of the Taxation Administration Act 1996 but subject to any restrictions in this Act.
See sections 374–376 of this Act.
In this section:
royalty information means information in a return lodged with the Chief Commissioner under this Act or any other information relating to the assessment or recovery of royalty.
tax officer has the same meaning as it has in the Taxation Administration Act 1996.
Subject to this section, a licence holder must pay a penalty to the Minister in respect of any fee that the holder fails to pay when it becomes payable.
The penalty is to be calculated:
on the amount of the fee that remains unpaid, and
at the rate of 0.33% for each day during which the fee is unpaid.
The State may recover the amount of any fee payable under this Part in a court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due to the State.
Royalty payable under this Act is a tax for the purposes of the Taxation Administration Act 1996.
The Taxation Administration Act 1996 applies to the assessment and recovery of royalty.
The royalty is payable to the Chief Commissioner in accordance with that Act.

The Minister is to ensure that the Chief Commissioner is provided with any information necessary to enable the Chief Commissioner to exercise the Chief Commissioner’s functions with respect to royalties under this Act and the Taxation Administration Act 1996.

heading.b: State functions under Part 5.1 of Commonwealth Act

block.txt: A State court may exercise any jurisdiction that is conferred on the court by the Commonwealth Act.
A State authority may perform any function that it is necessary for the authority to perform to give effect to Part 5.1 of the Commonwealth Act.
In this section:
State authority means:
the Governor,
a Minister of the Crown in right of the State,
a department of the Public Service of the State,
an agency, authority or instrumentality established under a written law of the State,
a person holding or exercising the powers of an office established under a written law of the State,
an officer or employee of:
an agency, authority or instrumentality referred to in paragraph (d), or
a person referred to in paragraph (e),
an officer appointed, or a person employed, under any other written law of the State,
any other person or entity prescribed by the regulations to be a State authority for the purposes of this section.

The Minister may by signed instrument delegate to a person the performance of all or any of the functions of the Minister under:
this Act, or
regulations made under this Act.

the lodgment of any document,
under this Act give any information or make any statement:

The Governor may make regulations prescribing all matters:

necessary or convenient to be prescribed for giving effect to this Act.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may provide for:
the control of offshore exploration and mining activities, and
procedures for giving notice to persons whose interests might be affected by the grant of a licence or special purpose consent, and
the conservation and protection of the mineral resources of coastal waters, and
the remedying of:
damage caused to the seabed or subsoil in coastal waters by offshore exploration and mining activities, or
damage caused by the escape of substances as a result of offshore exploration and mining activities, and
the protection of the environment, and
the keeping of records and samples, and
the giving of records and samples to the Minister for inspection, and
the making of returns, and
the imposition and recovery of fees,
without limiting paragraph (i), the determination by a specified person of any fees required or permitted to be prescribed by the regulations.
For “offshore exploration or mining activities” see section 5.
For the purposes of subsection (2), the control of offshore exploration and mining activities extends to the control of:
the construction, maintenance and operation of installations used in or for use in offshore exploration and mining activities, and
the flow or discharge of fluids arising from offshore exploration and mining activities, and
the safety, health and welfare of persons working in offshore exploration and mining activities, and
the maintenance of structures, equipment and property used in or for use in offshore exploration and mining activities.
For “offshore exploration or mining activities” see section 5.
For the purposes of subsection (2) (b), interests that might be affected by the grant of a licence include native title rights and interests that might be affected by the grant of the licence.
Subject to section 124, the regulations may provide for offences against the regulations.
The penalties provided for offences against the regulations are not to exceed:
a fine of $1 000, or
a fine of $1 000 for each day on which the offence is taken to continue.
In this section:
control includes restrict.
Subject to section 404, proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations may be disposed of in a summary manner before the Local Court.

heading.b: Provisions consequent on enactment of this Act

block.txt: An exploration licence in force under the Mining Act 1992 immediately before the commencement of this clause in relation to an area to which this Act applies is taken to be an exploration licence granted under this Act.

An application under the Mining Act 1992 for a renewal of an exploration licence in relation to an area to which this Act applies that has not been determined at the commencement of this clause is taken to be an application under this Act for the renewal of the licence.

An application under the Mining Act 1992 for an assessment lease in relation to an area to which this Act applies that has not been determined at the commencement of this clause is taken to be an application under this Act for a retention licence in respect of the same area.

An application under the Mining Act 1992 for a mining lease in relation to an area to which this Act applies that has not been determined at the commencement of this clause is taken to be an application under this Act for a mining licence in respect of the same area.

Any area that constitutes a block or part of a block in coastal waters, and that was reserved by an order in force under section 367 of the Mining Act 1992 immediately before the commencement of this clause, is taken to have been declared as a reserved block under section 18 of this Act.

Nothing in this clause or section 18 prevents the carrying out of activities in accordance with an exploration licence in force under the Mining Act 1992 immediately before the commencement of this clause in relation to an area referred to in subclause (1).

An entry in the register kept under section 161 of the Mining Act 1992 that relates to an area to which this Act applies must, after the commencement of this clause, be removed from that register and included in the offshore mining register kept under this Act.
